accuracy.evidence: Working-memory limits checked against Cowan (2001, about three to five chunks in adults) and Gathercole and Alloway (2008, children hold fewer items; overload shows as losing track of steps); the lab's four-space head is described in the text as 'only a few things', not as an exact span. Offloading claims match Risko and Gilbert (2016) on cognitive offloading. Teaching jottings and recording in-between results matches EEF Metacognition and self-regulated learning (2021) and EEF Improving Mathematics in Key Stages 2 and 3 (2017); two-step problems are in the National Curriculum (2013) for Years 3 and 4. All arithmetic checked: 3 × 6 = 18, 18 − 2 = 16, 5 × 4 = 20, 20 − 3 = 17, and every parameterised item at its range corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips named in the adult text: believing you can hold it all in your head (the fifth fact pushes the first one out of the head), copying the whole question (refused: 'buries the numbers'), jotting facts that do not change the answer (the colour and Monday cards are refused with their own reasons), adding instead of multiplying for 3 bags of 6 (9 refused) and counting only 2 bags (12 refused), starting step 2 from a number in the question (4 = 6 − 2 refused) or adding instead of taking away (20 refused), trying to think with a full head (Work it out refused until two spaces are free) and jotting bare numbers (labels must go on the right number).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagjot is built around a head with four spaces next to a jotter: facts dragged into the head push the oldest out when it is full, facts dragged onto the jotter stay, only facts that change Ria's answer can be jotted, number tiles for each step of a two-step problem go onto the jotter as in-between answers, a full head must be emptied onto the jotter before Work it out runs, and labels are dragged onto bare numbers. It is not 176 flagmem (chunking, forgetting curve, retrieval practice) or 1044 flagreadq (marking the ask in a question); the 6-token shingle gate reports no flag lab above 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers each idea by acting: putting the fifth fact in the head makes 'Swim club is on Thursday' drop out and return to the card, the jotter keeps everything; Work it out with a full head is refused and succeeds once facts are jotted; step 2 is solved by starting from the jotted 18. Each DONE line then states the rule (the page keeps what the head cannot; jot what matters; jot the in-between answer; jotting frees room to think; say what each number means).

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then disproves: 'Yes, easily' for holding 6 facts (the head drops one), 'Yes, copy it all' for jotting every word (the Copy the whole question card is refused), and 'Keep it in my head' for the in-between answer (step 2 only works from the jotted 18). The reveal line names the right answer after each task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge questions, each wrong option tied to a named slip: holding everything gets the overflow message, copying gets 'buries the numbers', starting from 6 or 3 gets 'start step 2 from the in-between answer, 18', '3 bags' as unneeded gets 'that fact changes the answer', 'more numbers' gets the label message, 'try harder' gets 'no room to think', a guess gets 'a guess is not working it out', 9 gets '3 × 6, not 3 + 6' and 12 gets 'only 2 bags of 6'. Checked by clicking through with chal.cjs.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores grade 1.5 (family limit 5.0): short sentences built on a concrete example (3 bags, 6 in each, eats 2) with the key term in-between answer used plainly. Adult text scores grade 7.7 (limit 10.0) and names working memory and cognitive offloading with one-line meanings. Canvas text is short: fact chips, 'In my head: 4 of 4', 'Jotter'.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one idea (the head holds only a few things; jot numbers and their meaning but not everything; jot the in-between answer; a full head has no room to think). Adult paragraphs give the research and curriculum basis, why children resist jotting, the named mistakes with the 6 − 2 versus 18 − 2 example, and what to do at home and in the lab. The content gate finds no filler phrase.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px phone screenshots in light and dark for all five scenes: fact chips wrap in rows inside the question card, the purple head bubble with four labelled spaces sits beside the ruled jotter, jotted lines use short forms (Thursday, £3, Gate B) so they fit one line, the step tiles are large and inside the head, Work it out sits under the head with the free-space count beside it, and the four bare numbers each have a full line for their label.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: 'Hold in my head' and 'Jot down' for each fact, 'Move from my head to the jotter', 'Jot: 3 bags' for each card, 'Step 1: jot 18' per tile, Work it out, and 'Put the label bags by the number 3'. The canvas aria-label carries each scene description and every piece of feedback, including which fact dropped out; challenge feedback is a role=status live region; ✓ and ✗ mark right and wrong as well as colour; axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) is clean in both themes.
